_comment: Dungeons and raids of WoW Forever for the addon's dungeon planner, kept by hand. tools/build_dungeons.py turns this file into addon/Amisia/DungeonData.lua. Facts only: names, level ranges, group sizes, bosses known so far, opening dates and instance ids; never a loot table, a drop chance or a list taken from a fan site. Each entry names its source in "src" (see "sources"). Fields: key (short id), name (English, as the item data names it), kind (party or raid), min/max (level range; null while unknown), size (players; null while unknown), inst (instance id; null until the client reports it through the drop records), area (area id), from (opening date), bosses (names known so far), aliases (other spellings the item data and quests use).

sources.forever: Public facts on WoW Forever's new dungeons and raids: names, level ranges, raid sizes and the raid opening on 2026-12-09 from Blizzard's announcements and the public dungeon list, bosses known so far from the same; checked by hand on 2026-10-05. Instance ids are left empty (Onyxia's Lair: see zones); the client reports them through the drop records.
sources.repo: Classic dungeons as the repo's own data names them: the dungeon sources and dungeon quests of addon/Amisia/GearData.lua (tools/build_gear.py) and the entrances of addon/Amisia/MapData.lua (tools/build_map.py). Their level ranges and sizes stay empty until the LFGDungeons client table (wago CSV, downloaded by hand) is read; meanwhile the addon estimates a range from the required levels of the dungeon's items and marks it as an estimate. The item data's plain "Blackrock Spire" records (War Master Voone, Goraluk Anvilcrack) belong to Lower Blackrock Spire, where those bosses stand.
sources.zones: Onyxia's Lair: instance id 249 and area id 2159 from tools/forever_zones.json.
